title: Thai government declares public holidays due to severe flooding
excerpt: Special holidays are set for September 28 and 29 in four provinces as heavy rainfall causes widespread flooding.
bodyHtml:
The Thai government has declared special public holidays on 28 and 29 September in Bangkok, Nonthaburi, Pathum Thani and Samut Prakan. This decision follows reports of severe flooding affecting parts of Thailand after heavy rainfall in these provinces.

According to the UK government, all 50 districts of Bangkok have been declared disaster-affected areas. The flooding has created the potential for travel disruption, including road closures and the inundation of low-lying areas across the region.

Many government offices and services in the affected provinces may be closed or operating with reduced capacity during this period. The UK government advises that individuals in the area should follow the guidance of local authorities if they plan to travel.

The government has designated September 28 and 29 as the dates for these special public holidays.
